name: Iranxe

catalog_locator: §1.1.3 Suprasegmental phonemes: opening sentence English p. 44 / Portuguese p. 12; stress paragraph English p. 45 / Portuguese p. 13; word definition §1.2.2 English p. 46 / Portuguese p. 14; footnotes 6 and 12: Port. pp. 35-36, Eng. pp. 65-66; secondary stress in compounds also §3.2.1.1 (Eng. p. 57).
catalog_quote: [Eng. p. 45] A phoneme of stress may occur on any syllable of a word. (6) It is indicated by ' preceeding the stressed syllable. Examples: šiki?'i anteater, ši'kiki comb, 'šĩkula (species of) parrot, 'ʌyalala (species of) snake, 'aⁱpʌ"mʌneti Where is it?. One or more secondary stresses occur on compound words. This stress is marked by " preceeding the stressed syllable. It occurs on the same syllable that is stressed in the simple noun from which the compound is derived. Examples: pe"šĩši'pewi flamevine {Cf. pe'šĩši humming bird}, "mãⁱnipa"tapa'Kãma shoe {Cf. "mãⁱnipa'tapa sole of foot and 'mãⁱni foot}. [Port. p. 13] O fonema de intensidade pode ocorrer em qualquer sílaba de um vocábulo (6). Indica-se por ' precedendo a sílaba acentuada. Exemplos: šiki?'i tamanduá, ši'kiki pente, 'šĩkula (espécie de) papagaio, 'ʌyalala (espécie de) cobra, 'aⁱpʌ"mʌneti Onde está?. [Eng. p. 46, §1.2.2] A word (defined as an expression having unitary primary stress, that may occur in isolation) consists of one or more syllables. ... Up to 8 syllables have been recorded. [Eng. p. 44, §1.1.3, opening] There are 3 suprasegmental phonemes in Iranxe. These are phonemes of nasalization, of length and of stress.

new_statements.quote: Há 3 fonemas supra-segmentais em Iranxe. São fonemas de nasalização, quantidade e intensidade. [...] O fonema de intensidade pode ocorrer em qualquer sílaba de um vocábulo (6). Indica-se por ' precedendo a sílaba acentuada. Exemplos: siki?'i tamanduá, si'kiki pente, 'sikula (espécie de) papagaio, 'Ayalala (espécie de) cobra, 'aipA"mAneti Onde está?. Um ou mais acentos secundários podem ocorrer em palavras compostas. Marca-se êsse acento por " precedendo a sílaba acentuada. Ocorre na mesma sílaba que é acentuada no nome simples do qual se deriva o composto. [English p. 45:] A phoneme of stress may occur on any syllable of a word. It is indicated by ' preceeding the stressed syllable.
new_statements.translation: There are 3 suprasegmental phonemes in Iranxe: phonemes of nasalization, length and stress. [...] The stress phoneme may occur on any syllable of a word. It is indicated by ' preceding the stressed syllable. Examples: siki?'i anteater, si'kiki comb, 'sikula (species of) parrot, 'Ayalala (species of) snake, 'aipA"mAneti Where is it?. One or more secondary stresses occur on compound words, marked by " before the stressed syllable; it falls on the same syllable that is stressed in the simple noun from which the compound is derived.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File opened: (144 PDF pages, Adobe Paper Capture text, etnolinguistica.org Curt Nimuendajú copy; the PDF's metadata gives the title 'Iranxe: notas gramaticais e lista vocabular', author Meader). Locators check out: Portuguese §1.1.3 begins on printed p. 12 (p. 15) 'Há 3 fonemas supra-segmentais em Iranxe. São fonemas de nasalização, quantidade e intensidade.' and continues on printed p. 13 (p. 16): 'O fonema de intensidade pode ocorrer em qualquer sílaba de um vocábulo (6). Indica-se por ' precedendo a sílaba acentuada. Exemplos: siki?'i tamanduá, si'kiki pente, 'sikula (espécie de) papagaio, 'Ayalala (espécie de) cobra, 'aipA"mAneti Onde está?. Um ou mais acentos secundários podem ocorrer…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is treated as a phoneme (contrastive 'intensity'), free to fall on any syllable of the word; no positional rule is given, and the examples show final (siki?'i), penultimate (si'kiki) and initial/antepenultimate ('sikula, 'Ayalala) stress. The word is defined as an expression with one primary stress that can occur in isolation. Vowels in unstressed h-initial syllables devoice; long vowels and complex vowels occur in stressed syllables.
new_statements.secondary_stress: One or more secondary stresses occur in compound words, marked with " and located on the syllable that bears primary stress in the corresponding simple noun (e.g. pe"sisi'pewi 'flamevine' from pe'sisi 'hummingbird'; "mãinipa"tapa'Kãma 'shoe' from "mãinipa'tapa 'sole of foot', 'mãini 'foot').
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; note 12 says intonation patterns were not satisfactorily analysed. The later Mỹky grammar (Monserrat 2010, via D'Angelis's review) treats the relation between pitch, duration and intensity as unresolved and gives unanalysed examples where pitch seems to contrast, so the 1967 stress analysis may be superseded by a pitch/tone analysis.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (vocábulo = expression with a single primary stress, occurring in isolation); compounds carry additional secondary stresses; based on the Irántxe (Manoki) speakers of the Cravari river, data 1947-1957 with a monolingual approach.
new_statements.identity_note: Meader 1967 describes the Irántxe (Manoki) group of the Cravari river (data 1947-1957, then ~43 speakers); Monserrat 2000/2010 and Bardagil 2023/2024 describe the Mỹky (Münkü) group contacted in 1971. Both are treated as one language under Glottolog iran1263 (Rodrigues; D'Angelis 2010: 'Mỹky e Irantxe falam uma mesma língua', groups separated early 20th c.). The stress statement therefore comes from the Irántxe/Manoki variety, while the modern Mỹky grammar leaves pitch vs. intensity unresolved; no separate Glottolog dialect codes were verified.
